_readme: Nights that never fall below 20 C, per European city, each against its own record. One thermometer per city, city warming included. Not a climate measurement and never presented as one.

definition.name: Tropical night
definition.rule: daily minimum temperature at or above 20.0 C
definition.standard: ETCCDI index TR, as published by European met services. Not a threshold we chose.

headline.may_not_say: 2026 is NOT the worst year on this measure. 2003 produced 12 on the same to-date basis and is inside living memory for this readership.
headline.the_better_story: Three of the four worst years on this measure are the last four years. A pattern rather than an event.
headline.caveat: 2026 is counted to 2-3 August with the season unfinished. Prior years are counted to the same date, so the comparison is like-for-like today, but 2026 can still add records before September.

rank.requires_series_note: This rank may not be rendered without the series below it. A bare rank is an alarm; the same rank beside its ordinary years is a calibrated statement, which is the only thing on the page we ask a reader not to take on trust.
rank.matched_note: Every prior year is counted to the same calendar day as 2026, so this is not a partial year against complete ones.

sources_note: All published sources permit commercial reuse. ECA&D is used for verification only, never as a published source, because it is non-commercial. Every city was verified day-by-day against its own independent historical record before use.
coverage_note: Spain and France. This metric does not work in northern Europe, where tropical nights are near zero and ratios divide by almost nothing.
